baseline_models.focus_anchor: قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَكَ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا مِن دُونِهِم
baseline_models.mechanism: The uttered tasbih clears God of the proposed association, while the wali and min dunihim construction denies a reciprocal alliance with the referenced group and states the speakers' actual allegiance before bal corrects the worship-object.

activation_trace.role: Overtly produced speech makes the clause testimonial rather than an unvoiced attitude.
Exonerating transcendence supplies the speech's rejection of the proposed association.
Alliance, love, and support define the relation the speakers affirm with God and deny with the human group.
The other-than or substitute relation makes the patronage claim exclusive rather than additive.

changed_reading.before: A praise formula followed by the naming of the speakers' true ally.
changed_reading.after: A spoken exoneration that denies reciprocal patronage with the humans and relocates the speakers' alliance exclusively with God before identifying the effective recipient of worship.

baseline_models.mechanism: Bal replaces the proposed recipient with al-jinn; kana presents the submissive practice as an established state, and the concealment field of j-n-n makes the correction disclose an effective object lying beneath the claimed relation.

activation_trace.role: Occurrence through time casts the worship as an established prior condition, not a momentary error.
Submissive worship and obedience specify the practical allegiance being diagnosed.
The concealed jinn are the literal class installed as the corrected object of worship.
Concealment supplies the diagnostic mechanism: the effective recipient is disclosed from beneath a mistaken attribution.

changed_reading.before: They worshipped jinn rather than the speakers.
changed_reading.after: The correction exposes an established allegiance beneath the professed relation: submissive practice ran to concealed beings, while the named speakers deny having received it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: كَانُوا۟ يَعْبُدُونَ ٱلْجِنَّ ۖ أَكْثَرُهُم بِهِم مُّؤْمِنُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: The first clause predicates worship of the group, whereas the second restricts settled belief to most of them. Numerical majority and heart-settled credence make the second clause an audit of inward penetration rather than a redundant restatement.

activation_trace.role: Submissive practice supplies the broader collective behavior.
Numerical abundance marks a majority while leaving a remainder outside the qualification.
Heart-settled assent specifies the inward conviction attained by most participants.

changed_reading.before: Worship and belief repeat the same accusation in two forms.
changed_reading.after: Collective submissive practice is broader than settled conviction: most, but not necessarily every participant, internalized trust in the jinn.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same jinn are first presented as workers acting by permission and later exposed as not knowing the unseen. The focus therefore describes an inverted hierarchy: humans submit to concealed beings who are themselves subordinate laborers with bounded authorization and failed hidden knowledge.

activation_trace.role: The concealed jinn remain the literal focus object whose rank is being reassessed.
Submissive obedience supplies the downward human-to-jinn relation that the context inverts.
The same concealed class appears inside a labor arrangement rather than as an autonomous patron.
Purposive work assigns the jinn a worker role in the supplied hierarchy.
Permission and authorization bound that work under a superior will.
Knowledge as disclosure is placed in an unreal condition and thereby denied to the jinn.
The unseen is the concealed domain they fail to know, separating hidden existence from hidden knowledge.

structural_cues: 34:12 places al-jinn in a partitive construction before a work verb and a permission phrase.
34:14 makes al-jinn the subject of a disclosure and puts knowing the unseen inside an unreal condition.
34:41 reverses that subordinate class into the object of human worship.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies jinn working by permission and their disclosed failure to know the unseen; I infer that a permission-bound, ignorant worker cannot be the final patron the worshippers treat it as. A live alternative is that these verses establish jinn subordination without specifying what the humans expected from them.

changed_reading.before: The focus merely substitutes jinn for the apparently addressed recipients.
changed_reading.after: The substitution is hierarchical irony: people submitted to hidden beings who were themselves controlled, punishable workers and not masters of hidden knowledge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah sets a few grateful servants against a majority, then shows a conjecture realized through followership while denying the followed figure any coercive authority. The focus's worship-belief pair becomes a diagnostic distribution of voluntary allegiance: most settle into the following, while a believing faction remains distinct.

activation_trace.role: Numerical abundance in the focus supplies the captured majority.
Settled assent identifies what has taken hold in that majority.
Explicit fewness supplies the numerical counterweight to the focus's most.
The few are located among God's submissive servants, furnishing an alternative allegiance.
Realization of a prior expectation links conjecture to its behavioral fulfillment.
Conjecture and imagining characterize the script that the followers make effective.
Following as allegiance supplies a concrete mechanism by which worship operates.
A separated faction preserves the minority exception within the wider following.
Settled belief marks the excepted faction on the opposite side of the sorting.
The explicit absence of power or authority prevents the following from being explained as coercion.
Interpenetrating doubt supplies the unstable alternative that the test distinguishes from belief.

structural_cues: 34:13 says few among My servants, while 34:41 says most of them.
34:20 expresses followership with an exception for a believing faction.
34:21 negates authority and states a purpose of distinguishing belief from doubt.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies numerical contrast, following, an excepted believing faction, no coercive authority, and a belief-versus-doubt test; I infer that the focus records voluntary capture by allegiance rather than forced compliance. Ritual worship may still coexist with this followership mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Most participants added inward belief to a broader collective practice.
changed_reading.after: Most participants were sorted into settled jinn-allegiance by following a conjectural script without coercion, while a small believing-servant minority remained outside it.

context_deltas.mechanism: Calling those claimed apart from God is followed by a systematic removal of ownership, share, support, benefit, and independent intercession. The focus's wali claim therefore concerns real jurisdiction and access, not sentiment alone; bal exposes concealed jinn as the beneficiary of a failed substitute-access chain.

activation_trace.role: Alliance and support anchor the focus in an actual patronage relation.
Other-than or substitute status marks the competing relation denied by the speakers.
Calling by speech supplies the attempted access action directed to claimed others.
An assertion without certainty weakens the claimed status of those invoked.
The exact substitute relation recurs around the invoked figures and links directly to the focus.
Ownership and power of disposal are explicitly denied, removing jurisdiction from the substitutes.
Participation or share is denied, closing a joint-authority route.
Back-strengthening aid is denied, closing a support route.
Benefit is the expected positive capacity that the passage makes unavailable on its own.
A mediator joining another supplies the last possible access link.
Permission subordinates even mediation to authorization and removes independent access.

structural_cues: 34:22 repeats min duni, the focus's substitute-relation construction.
The sequence moves from invocation through ownership, share, aid, benefit, and intercession.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an invocation followed by negated capacities and permission-bound mediation; I infer that worshippers sought protection or access through a substitute chain and that 34:41 identifies its concealed beneficiary. A live alternative is submission without any expected benefit or intercession.

changed_reading.before: The speakers say God, not the humans, is their ally.
changed_reading.after: The speakers deny an entire patronage-and-access transaction: the proposed recipients possess no reciprocal jurisdiction, while effective devotion has flowed to concealed jinn through the failed chain.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier exchange returns accusation between weak and arrogant parties; later all are driven together, the angels are directly asked whether they received worship, and the next verse rules out mutual benefit or harm. The focus is thus witness testimony in an adjudication of agency, recipient, and capacity.

activation_trace.role: Repeated overt speech stages reciprocal accusation as testimony rather than private blame.
Driving and collecting a group to a destination supplies the hearing's compulsory assembly.
Complete gathering makes the questioned population comprehensive rather than selective.
The spoken divine question elicits the focus response as direct testimony.
The angel branch identifies the questioned party whose alleged receipt of worship is at issue.
The repeated temporal-state verb frames the question about an established past practice.
The identical submissive-worship branch states the charge that 34:41 corrects.
The focus utterance functions as the witnesses' answer within that exchange.
Exoneration gives the testimony a formal disavowal before it reallocates the worship-object.
The verdict removes every party's power of disposal over another.
Benefit names one patronal capacity that no gathered party can deliver.
Harm names the opposite capacity that is equally unavailable.

structural_cues: 34:31-33 stage returned speech and responsibility-shifting between social groups.
34:40 asks إِيَّاكُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْبُدُونَ and 34:41 answers with بَلْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْبُدُونَ ٱلْجِنَّ.
34:42 immediately converts the testimony into a capacity verdict.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies blame-dialogue, total gathering, a direct worship question, an answer, and a no-capacity verdict; I infer that the focus allocates effective recipient and responsibility as forensic evidence. The answer can remain doxological while also serving this adjudicative role.

changed_reading.before: The verse is a free-standing doctrinal denial by the speakers.
changed_reading.after: It is elicited witness testimony: the angels reject receipt, identify the concealed effective recipient, and thereby prepare the verdict that none of the parties owns benefit or harm.

context_deltas.mechanism: Night-and-day command installs rival counterparts, while inherited worship is defended and the incoming truth is dismissed through reversal and deception language. These social and rhetorical channels make it possible for devotion to be consciously framed as ancestral practice while its effective concealed object is diagnosed as jinn.

activation_trace.role: Concealment anchors the claim that the effective recipient need not match the devotees' overt framing.
The literal jinn remain the named hidden agents; the social mechanism does not replace them.
Command and obligation supply a human channel that directs people toward rival-making.
A rival counterpart names the publicly installed object through which allegiance is organized.
Submissive worship recurs as the practice attributed to the fathers.
Fatherhood and upbringing supply intergenerational transmission for that practice.
Falsehood turned away from truth characterizes the narrative used to preserve inherited worship.
Diversion and deception supply a second rhetorical defense against disclosure.

structural_cues: 34:33 places command under the continuous frame of night and day before making rivals.
34:43 repeats kana plus worship for the fathers immediately after the focus hearing.
34:43 surrounds inherited worship with three public sayings that reclassify the challenger and the truth.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies elite command, rival-making, inherited worship, and truth-reversing labels; I infer that these are channels through which concealed jinn receive effective obedience without requiring every devotee to name them consciously. Direct and conscious jinn worship remains a live alternative.

changed_reading.before: The group knowingly addresses jinn as its explicit cult object.
changed_reading.after: Jinn-directed obedience may be socially mediated through commanded rivals, inherited practice, and truth-reversing narratives, so the conscious label and the effective recipient can diverge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's dun can carry nearness short of the goal, while the ending contrasts seizure from a near place with a declaration of belief that cannot reach from a far place and is finally blocked by a barrier. Belief in the jinn becomes misplaced proximity: trust settles on nearer substitutes but leaves genuine belief inaccessible when disclosure arrives.

activation_trace.role: Nearness that falls short of the goal supplies the focus's latent spatial relation.
Settled assent anchors the spatial model in the focus's actual act of believing in them.
Failure of attainment closes escape at the moment of exposure.
Seizure and capture make the near location operational rather than merely descriptive.
Nearness locates the effective grasp that reaches them.
The same settled-assent branch now voices late belief in it, contrasting with prior belief in them.
Reaching by extension supplies the access that is impossible from the stated distance.
Distance opposite nearness locates the failed attempt at belief.
An intervening barrier turns spiritual distance into blocked access.
Interpenetrating doubt names the unstable state maintained before the barrier.
Agitated suspicion intensifies that distance from settled true assent.

structural_cues: 34:51-53 repeat makan with near, far, and far in successive verses.
34:41 has بهم مؤمنون, while 34:52 answers with آمنا به after exposure.
34:54 concludes with a barrier between the people and what they seek.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies dun's near-but-short branch, settled belief in them, and an ending organized by near seizure, far reaching, and a barrier; I infer a topology in which false trust chooses proximate substitutes but produces distance from recoverable true belief. Min dunihim may still function simply as apart from them, so the spatial reading is supplementary.

changed_reading.before: Min dunihim only excludes the humans from the speakers' alliance, and belief in the jinn is purely propositional.
changed_reading.after: The exclusion also activates a failed-distance map: nearer substitutes receive settled trust, yet that trust leaves the worshippers too far away to reach belief when it matters.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it moves from al-jinn as beings to the j-n-n shield branch and then to the surah's material armor sequence. It remains anchored in the focus's jinn and wali roots and in the post-focus benefit-harm test. Downstream prose should present it only as a protective-function analogy, never as a replacement gloss for al-jinn.

activation_trace.role: Alliance and support supply the protective function explicitly claimed for God.
The protective shield image recasts the expected function of the jinn as imagined cover.
Ample extension until a thing is covered supplies the armor's enveloping protection.
Pierced links joined together provide the material mechanism of a real fabricated shield.
Denied benefit tests and fails the supposed protective function of substitute patrons.
Denied control of harm completes the failure of the imagined shield.

changed_reading.before: The verse names hidden beings as the object of worship and God as the speakers' ally.
changed_reading.after: As a material analogy, devotees treated jinn as a metaphysical shield, but the speakers deny that protective function and reserve actual guardianship for God.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it crosses from the noun naming jinn beings to the same root's mind-covering madness branch. It remains valid as a functional overlay because the surah repeats jinnah beside a command to reflect, while the focus keeps the literal jinn branch in view. Downstream prose must qualify it as an analogy for cognition captured by concealed prompting, not claim that al-jinn lexically means madness here.

activation_trace.role: The concealed jinn supply the indispensable literal anchor for the exploratory overlay.
Covering of reason opens a cognitive function associated with the same root.
An explicit madness occurrence activates the root's mind-covering domain elsewhere in the surah.
The heart's repeated consideration supplies the reflective process opposed to cognitive covering.
Negated madness immediately after the reflection command makes that opposition locally visible.

changed_reading.before: The worship is direct devotion to a class of concealed beings.
changed_reading.after: Without displacing that literal object, the worship can also figure devotion to concealed prompts that cover reflection and secure assent before scrutiny.

strongest_changes: The jinn labor and ignorance sequence turns their worship into an inverted hierarchy rather than merely a wrong label.
The few-most contrast, followership, and absence of coercive authority make majority belief a voluntary diagnostic capture.
The invocation, ownership, aid, and permission sequence turns wali into jurisdiction and access, while the hearing makes the focus formal witness testimony.
Commanded rivals and inherited worship allow the conscious social frame to diverge from the concealed effective recipient.
The near-far ending activates a supplementary topology of misplaced trust in nearer substitutes.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly reuses exact focus roots and constructions on both sides of 34:41: jinn as workers, failed knowers, and a madness-root occurrence; most against few; min dun for claimed substitutes; kana plus worship in the question and ancestral practice; and belief in them against late belief in it. Those recurrences produced causal, juridical, social, and spatial mechanisms rather than a topical catalog.
remaining_uncertainties: The precise antecedent of him in min dunihim and the degree of conscious jinn-identification among the worshippers remain open within the focus syntax.
Direct cult, elite mediation, and inherited practice can coexist; the packet does not force one channel.
The distance, shield, and cognitive-covering activations are branch-led analogies and must not replace the focus's ordinary lexical reading.
